samples.summary: `durable` is never supplied to `deriveSyncState`, so the new `saved-locally` chip state is unreachable
samples.evidence: `sync-state.ts` gains a `durable?` signal and `sync-status-chip.tsx` gains a label, icon and tooltip for `saved-locally`, but `useSyncStatus` — the only caller of `deriveSyncState` in the app — still calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed })` with no `durable`, which defaults to `false`. The design doc states the provider computes `durable` and supplies it through context, and that the fourth row dropping from destructive to muted 'is the entire user-facing value of this feature' (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § What the user sees). As shipped a document can be durable while the chip still says 'Not saved' and the tooltip still tells the user their edits 'exist only in this tab' — a false statement about a persisted document, and a violation of the doc's `durable ⇒ reportable` invariant.

samples.summary: No opt-in control ships anywhere: neither the Settings switch nor the chip entry point, so the feature cannot be turned on
samples.evidence: The design specifies two entry points — a Settings switch beside Appearance/Dates, and an offer from the sync chip (§ Turning it on) — and the rollout table puts 'the Settings + chip opt-in' in the same PR as wiring the store. `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled` is called only from its own tests; grep for 'offline' in packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx returns nothing. The store, election and durable provider are wired into `CollabDocumentProvider`, but no user can reach any of it — the stated outcome ('edits made while disconnected survive a reload ... on a device where the user has asked for it') is unattainable.

samples.summary: `watchForOfflineDisable` is never started, so the toggle's central promise — 'turning this off deletes them' — is unkept
samples.evidence: `offline-erase.ts` exists with its own suite, but grep shows no importer outside `offline-erase.test.ts`. The design states 'Turning it off erases. Disabling drops every stored entry for that user on that device, including archived envelopes. A toggle that left the content behind would not be the control it presents itself as' (§ Turning it on). With no call site, disabling the preference merely stops new writes and leaves every previously stored document — full compressed content — on the device's disk until the 30-day sweep, which is itself unwired (see the cleanup finding).
searchedFor: grep offline-erase across packages/frontend/src excluding tests

samples.summary: The offline-copy recovery path has no caller, so archived unreconcilable work is never returned to the user
samples.evidence: Goal: 'Work that genuinely cannot be reconciled with the server is returned to the user as a document, not a console log', and § Losing work anyway specifies the user is told what happened with a link to the copy. `recoverOfflineCopy` and `listRecoverableWork` are imported only by their own tests. The store dutifully archives on a latched loss, but nothing lists or rehydrates archives in the app, so the archived bytes sit in IndexedDB until the (also unwired) 30-day collection deletes them — the goal is unmet and the archive is currently pure cost.

samples.summary: None of the documented cleanup triggers (logout, document deleted/access lost, 30-day sweep) are wired to the store
samples.evidence: The doc's cleanup table (§ Storage) lists Logout → drop every entry for that user; document deleted or workspace access lost → drop that entry; Periodic → drop entries untouched for 30 days. `dropAllForUser`, `purge` and `collectStale` are implemented and tested, but grep finds no non-test caller anywhere in `packages/frontend/src` (nav-user.tsx's logout does not touch the store). Stored document content therefore outlives sign-out on a shared machine — the exact scenario the whole opt-in design is built around — and nothing ever reclaims quota.

samples.summary: `durable` is computed from the election alone, omitting the two other terms the design requires
samples.evidence: § What the user sees: "`durable` is the conjunction of three facts: this tab won the app lock, no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off, and the store is not failing its writes." `useDurableDocument` returns `durable = answered && !!decision?.session` — the election only. The store's write failures (the quota-exhausted and `evicted` rejection paths it carefully implements) and any `PersistDisabled` latch never feed back into the signal, so the documented failure-reason table (out of local storage space, could not save to this device, too large) has nothing behind it. No user impact today only because `durable` is not plumbed to the chip at all.

samples.summary: `documentIdOf` duplicates `documentKeyOf`, the exact single-source rule the store file argues for
samples.evidence: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts` exports `documentKeyOf` with the comment 'Defined here because this module is where store keys are consumed, and two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false.' `offline-copy.ts` then defines a byte-identical private `documentIdOf` (split on '/', take last segment) rather than importing it, so the rule now has two implementations that can diverge — the precise failure that comment documents.

samples.summary: A vitest-importing suite lives in `src/lib/` as a production module rather than under a test path
samples.evidence: `doc-store-contract.ts` imports `describe/it/expect` from 'vitest' and defines test cases, but sits in `packages/frontend/src/lib/` alongside shipped modules rather than in `tests/` or as a `*.test.ts`. The transcription itself is well justified (the SDK publishes only `dist`), but filing it as an ordinary `src` module puts a dev-only dependency on the production import graph and is a layering mismatch with the rest of the package's test placement.

samples.summary: The design's explicit React-key trap for the nested provider is not implemented as written
samples.evidence: § Client identity: "the provider must be given a React key covering both the document and the preference — key={`${docKey}:${enabled}`}", because `YorkieProvider` memoizes its client on `[apiKey, rpcAddr]` only. `DurableYorkieProvider` is rendered with no React key. In practice the `!settled` early-return appears to unmount the subtree on a document or preference change, which may achieve the same effect, but the divergence from the documented mechanism is undocumented and relies on a subtle timing property rather than the stated guard.

finding.summary: `durable` is never supplied to `deriveSyncState`, so the new `saved-locally` chip state is unreachable
finding.evidence: `sync-state.ts` gains a `durable?` signal and `sync-status-chip.tsx` gains a label, icon and tooltip for `saved-locally`, but `useSyncStatus` — the only caller of `deriveSyncState` in the app — still calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed })` with no `durable`, which defaults to `false`. The design doc states the provider computes `durable` and supplies it through context, and that the fourth row dropping from destructive to muted 'is the entire user-facing value of this feature' (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § What the user sees). As shipped a document can be durable while the chip still says 'Not saved' and the tooltip still tells the user their edits 'exist only in this tab' — a false statement about a persisted document, and a violation of the doc's `durable ⇒ reportable` invariant.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is factually correct and I found no counterexample after searching wide. `deriveSyncState` has exactly one non-test caller in the whole repo — use-sync-status.ts:214 — and it passes `{ connected, pending, syncFailed }` only, so `durable` falls back to `false` (sync-state.ts:70) and the `saved-locally` branch (sync-state.ts:85) can never be taken, despite the chip having a full label/icon/tooltip for it (sync-status-chip.tsx:41,52,64-79). `useSyncStatus` reads only `useDocument()` (line 68) and consumes no durability context. The durability machinery exists (lib/use-durable-document.ts:141,155-164) and collab-document-provider.tsx:158,185 consumes `durable` solely to decide whether to nest `DurableYorkieProvider`; it publishes nothing to the chip. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for durable|saved-locally|savedLocally|isDurable shows no edge between the two subsystems. The repo's own task file confirms the gap as unfinished work: docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:95-99 (task 3.5 unchecked), :128 (task 5.3 unchecked), and :175 ("`durable` in `use-sync-status.ts` | so the chip cannot reach `saved-locally`"). Under the design-fit rubric this is major: the design's stated user-facing value — the fourth row dropping from destructive to muted — is unreachable, an acceptance criterion left unmet. Mitigation worth recording for the merge discussion: the durable path is additionally dark because supportsClientKey() gates on a dependency version (yorkie-capabilities.ts:61-67) and setOfflinePersistenceEnabled has no production caller (only tests), so no user can currently see a durable document mislabelled "Not saved"; that blunts the false-statement harm but not the missing-behavior one, and is not a counterexample.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `recoverOfflineCopy` (offline-copy-recovery.ts:114) and `listRecoverableWork`/`rehydrateArchive` (offline-copy.ts:58,115) are referenced nowhere outside their own tests in a repo-wide search, and behavior-based searches (offline copy, archive, recover, "could not be saved", unsent) surface no UI, route, or hook that offers archived work back. verdict.reason: Verified independently. The design doc's cleanup table (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:212-217) does specify Logout → drop all entries for the user, document deleted/access lost → drop that entry, and Periodic → drop entries untouched 30 days. The store implements all three (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:717 purge, :795 dropAllForUser, :817 collectStale, :141 DefaultMaxAgeMs), but none is reached from application code: repo-wide grep shows collectStale only in *.test.ts files (no scheduler anywhere — no non-test hit for 30 * 24/maxAgeMs/sweep), purge only in the store's own internal calls (:798, :834, :847, :995) and tests with no document-delete/access-loss caller (api/documents.ts and app/documents/document-list.tsx never reference the store), and logout (api/auth.ts:80-110, invoked by components/nav-user.tsx:40-42) does nothing but POST, toast and redirect — no IndexedDB access at all. The one near-counterexample is lib/offline-erase.ts:30, which does call dropAllForUser from non-test code, but it serves the *preference-toggle-off* trigger rather than any of the three rows, and it has no production importer either (grep for offline-erase/eraseOfflineData/watchForOfflineDisable across packages returns only the module and its test). The repo's own planning doc corroborates: docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:169-175 states every listed module "has no production caller", with the explicit row "collectStale / dropAllForUser / purge | no sweep, no logout erase, no delete/access-loss cleanup". Not out-of-scope: the diff space includes the W3-W5 wiring modules (offline-erase.ts, durable-yorkie-provider.tsx, use-durable-document.ts, collab-document-provider.tsx), which is exactly where these triggers belong, so this is a documented acceptance item left unmet rather than deferred work outside the change.
